applied.problem: Steepness only shows ohms when lines share the same axes and scales; a resistor is proportional only while its resistance holds; the heater's bend sat beside 'not ohmic' as if linked; screens 9-10 put current up the side, so not the whole lesson follows Bitesize.

Comparing steepness needs the same axes and scales, and a best-fit line through real measured readings rarely passes exactly through (0, 0), so asking only whether it runs through (0, 0) would wrongly reject proportional data.
The 5 Ω heater is also drawn with a fixed resistance, but a real heater element's resistance changes as it warms; ignores names only the resistors as held constant.

notes.problem: Every number (the ohms, the £40 and £30, the drum, heater, part, tank and the measured readings) is an example value chosen for the lesson, as ignores says, so its kind is "assumed" (or "computed" from its rule), not "constant".
